The cargo crew and kennel doors, minutes
It started on time, and the front-counter lead led

Attendees were Grace Berg, Rina Silva, and Rosie.

The team reviewed the usual flow at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, starting with check-in notes, carrier condition, and the handoff between the counter and kennel area. Staff agreed that calm handling remains the standard in every exchange, with slow movements, steady voices, and clear spacing used to keep animals settled. The group also noted that any change to a booking, travel note, or care instruction must be written into the desk ledger at once so the next shift has a clean record.

The counter lead reported that most routine cases are moving smoothly, though a few travelers still need clearer reminders about carrier size, water access, and the need to arrive early enough for screening without crowding the desk. The team discussed how to give those reminders in a firm but friendly way, using plain language and repeating the key points when needed. Rosie was mentioned as a good example of how a calm pet can set the tone for a smooth check-in when the handler keeps the process unhurried.

Staff also reviewed kennel care basics, including visual checks, water refreshes, and confirming that labels match the travel notes before transfer. The discussion stayed focused on practical habits rather than new policy, and the group agreed that small errors are best caught early by reading back the booking details and comparing them with the physical tag. The front-counter lead asked everyone to keep the desk area uncluttered so forms, leashes, and carrier slips are easy to reach without delay.

Aurelia Skyways
The meeting ended in good order, with the next shift briefed and the desk ready for routine service.
